dedupe_keys.name: pysolar solar position and irradiation library

description: Pysolar is a Python library maintained by Brandon Stafford and contributors for calculating solar position and irradiation at a location on Earth. Users provide geographic coordinates and timezone-aware dates or times and obtain solar quantities for further analysis. Coverage is global, while temporal sampling follows the user's calls, not a fixed weather-observation series. The repository links function documentation and provides pip installation instructions. Public source is free under GPL-3.0. A limitation is the distinction between astronomical irradiation calculations and measured local weather: this resource does not supply cloud observations or a calibrated photovoltaic plant. The README also documents breaking changes from Python 2-era releases and warns that naive timestamps can produce incorrect results. Those interface details matter when reproducing older studies. Pysolar can prepare solar inputs for building or renewable-generation simulations, complementing EnergyPlus (model-energyplus) and broader power-system scenario models. The maintainer describes the project as a community-maintained library, not a supported commercial product. This review did not execute ephemeris calculations or compare numerical results with observations.
